title: Typical hyperbolic surfaces have a spectral gap greater than $2/9 - ε$
summary: In this article, we prove that typical hyperbolic surfaces, sampled with the Weil-Petersson probability measure, have a spectral gap at least $2/9 - ε$. This is an intermediate result on the way to our proof of the optimal spectral gap $1/4 - ε$, building on the results of the first part of this series. A significant part of the proof is an explicit inclusion-exclusion argument to exclude tangles at the level of precision $1/g$.
